title: ふと — suddenly, on an impulse
summary: An adverb for doing or noticing something suddenly, with no particular reason or plan. It is followed by actions of noticing, recalling, or glancing.

body.p: ふと describes something that happens suddenly and without a plan: ふと思い出す (suddenly recall), ふと気づく (notice), ふと見ると (when I happened to look). It fits near-unconscious actions like recalling, noticing and glancing.
突然 is for abrupt events; ふと is for a thought or small action that arises unexpectedly. It is not used with deliberate actions such as studying or shopping.

examples.ja: ふと窓（まど）の外（そと）を見（み）ると、雪（ゆき）が降（ふ）っていた。
examples.romaji: Futo mado no soto o miru to, yuki ga futte ita.
examples.tr: When I happened to glance outside, it was snowing.

examples.ja: ふと子（こ）どもの頃（ころ）のことを思（おも）い出（だ）した。
examples.romaji: Futo kodomo no koro no koto o omoidashita.

examples.ja: 歩（ある）いていると、ふといい考（かんが）えが浮（う）かんだ。
examples.romaji: Aruite iru to, futo ii kangae ga ukanda.
examples.tr: While walking, a good idea suddenly came to me.

pitfalls: Do not use it with deliberate actions: ふと勉強した sounds wrong.
It is not the same as 突然. For big events such as an earthquake, use 突然.
